conventions: spine-wire v1 conformance vectors. Generated by scripts/wire_v1.py from docs/spec/00-wire.md; do not edit by hand.
Regenerate: python scripts/wire_v1.py generate > docs/spec/00-wire.vectors.json. Check: python scripts/wire_v1.py check docs/spec/00-wire.vectors.json.
All 'hex' strings are lowercase, no spaces or prefix. A frame is u32 length, u8 version, u8 type, u8 flags, u64 request id (all big-endian), then the body.
Value descriptions: a JSON object is a CBOR map with text keys; arrays, strings, true, false and null are as in JSON.
A JSON number with a '.' or an exponent is a CBOR float; any other JSON number is a CBOR integer.
{"$bytes": "<hex>"} is a CBOR byte string. {"$int": "<decimal>"} is an integer beyond +-2^53 (JSON numbers are inexact there).
{"$float": "nan"|"inf"|"-inf"} is a float JSON cannot write. {"$map": [[key, value], ...]} is a map whose keys are not all text.
valid_bodies: deterministic CBOR items a decoder must accept. 'hex' is the exact encoding; 'value' describes it.
invalid_bodies: items a decoder must reject. 'reason' is the Rust cbor::CborError variant name, which is also the rule broken (C.5).

valid_frames: whole frames. 'type', 'request_id', 'flags' and 'body' (or 'body_hex') describe 'hex'. 'typed' names the body type that decodes it: command, auth_request, receipt, reply, ping, pong, stream, hello, hello_ack, identify, close, ext, or none (decode and re-encode of the typed value is not offered, e.g. a result with byte strings).

A frame with flags 1 has the body u32 uncompressed_len, then a zstd frame. These vectors store the body in a raw-block zstd frame (valid zstd, not smaller). A receiver must decode them to 'body_hex'; they are not byte-for-byte what a compressing sender would emit, so re-encoding is not part of the check.

invalid_frames: whole frames (or the prefix needed to decide) that a receiver using 'max_frame' as the maximum in force must reject with 'error' (the Rust frame::FrameError variant) and 'close_code' (C.7 wire text). 'build' re-derives 'hex'. incomplete_frames: valid prefixes; 'needed' is the least number of further bytes (FrameError::NeedMore).
The order of the stateless frame checks is: length, version, type, flags, request id, then the body (specification section 7.2).

handshakes: 'hello_frame' is a whole HELLO frame, 'local' the server configuration (with the per-connection 'binding' as hex, 'authority' and 'time', which a real server draws fresh and a vector fixes), 'expect' the outcome of validating the HELLO and negotiating: an 'ack' (with the whole 'ack_frame') or a 'close' with its code and 'supported'. CLOSE 'message' text is not specified and not part of a vector.
hello_acks: HELLO_ACK bodies ('body_hex', described by 'body') that a client accepts ('expect' ok) or refuses with the CLOSE code in 'expect' (section 6.3).

identify: an IDENTIFY body ('body_hex') judged against the connection whose HELLO and HELLO_ACK bodies are 'hello_body' and 'ack_body'. 'expect' is 'valid' or the CLOSE code. A valid vector also gives the test 'seed' (Ed25519 signatures are deterministic), the proven 'key', the signed 'message' M (section 6.6) and the 'signature'.

identify_sessions: 'hello_frame' and 'local' make a handshake; the server then receives the 'frames' (hex) in order. 'expect' is {result: ok, identity: hex or null} when all are accepted and the stream then ends, or {result: close, code} at the first one refused.

name_results: a RESPONSE 'ok' value for resolve_name (section 12.5), 'body_hex' described by 'body'. 'expect' is 'ok' or 'invalid' (the body is not a name resolution a decoder accepts). Entries of a succession log are checked for shape only: their signatures are not part of the wire layer.

ed25519_strict: 'public', 'message' and 'signature' (hex) with the verdict of plain RFC 8032 verification ('plain') and of verify_strict ('strict'); a conforming server uses the strict one (section 6.6).

delete_proofs: the proof of a delete_resource request (section 12.2). 'owner', 'hash', 'binding' (the connection's HELLO_ACK binding) and 'proof' are hex; 'expect' is 'valid' when strict Ed25519 verification of the message "spine-wire-delete-resource-v1" 00 || hash || binding under 'owner' accepts, else 'invalid'. A valid vector also gives the test 'seed' (signatures are deterministic) and the signed 'message'. The daemon's order is: verify the proof first (a failure is delete_refused), then look the blob up under 'owner'.
invalid_commands: REQUEST bodies ('body_hex', described by 'body') that a daemon answers with the error code 'code' (invalid_request or unknown_command, sections 7.4, 12.1, 12.2).

delete_results: the ok value of a delete reply (section 12.4), 'body_hex' described by 'body', for the command named in 'command'. 'expect' is 'ok' or 'invalid' (a closed map {deleted}: a boolean for delete_resource, an unsigned integer for delete_knowledge).

auth_requests: AUTH_REQUEST bodies (section 8.5), 'body_hex' described by 'body'. 'expect' is 'ok' or the answer code (invalid_request or unknown_command). An 'ok' vector also gives the 'command_hex' (the encoding of the command item) and 'op', its SHA-256, which is what an invocation's op field must equal.

receipts: RECEIPT bodies (section 8.6) of 'length' bytes. 'expect' is 'ok' or 'invalid' (not the closed map {body: map, sig: 64 bytes}, or over 512 bytes). Signatures and contents are not judged here.
result_digests: the 'digest' a receipt carries as its result for a RESPONSE body: SHA-256 of "spine-wire-result-v1" 00 and 'body_hex' (section 8.6).

error_codes: the closed list of codes a v1 daemon produces (section 13) in the order of its table, with their 'count' and the three 'protocol' codes. check also compares it with the table in docs/spec/00-wire.md.
A vector with a 'note' explains the rule it exercises and cites the section of docs/spec/00-wire.md that states it.
Not covered: connection state other than the IDENTIFY window (id reuse, direction, HELLO first, extension index, timeouts, max_inflight) and real zstd compression.
